extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and policy-makers interested in peer review and Open Science
extracted.subtask_description: Systematically collect and classify definitions and features of 'open peer review' (OPR) from the literature to produce a coherent typology of OPR traits and configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of reviewer and/or author identities
rubrics_metrics.description: OPR as peer review where the identities of both author and reviewer are disclosed to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract states that for some definitions the term refers specifically to identity disclosure. This trait is one of the core features the review quantifies when building the typology of OPR definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems where reviewer reports are published alongside articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many definitions treat publication of reports as a defining feature; the paper quantifies how frequently this trait appears across the 122 collected definitions and includes it in the proposed umbrella definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open participation / wider commenting (beyond invited experts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems where not only 'invited experts' are able to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some uses of OPR emphasize enabling greater participation in the peer review process by widening who can comment; the review treats this as a distinct trait when mapping configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations of OPR traits (multiple configurations)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPR frequently denotes various combinations of features (e.g., identity disclosure plus published reports, plus open participation); the literature shows overlapping and contradictory definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study assembled 122 definitions and found 22 distinct configurations of seven traits — i.e., many definitions are hybrid. Evaluations or implementations should therefore specify which trait-combinations they mean rather than assuming a single definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPR as umbrella term aligned with Open Science aims
rubrics_metrics.description: A pragmatic definition treating OPR as an umbrella term for overlapping ways peer review models can be adapted in line with the aims of Open Science (including identity openness, report publication, and greater participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author proposes this pragmatic umbrella to capture the diversity of practices; implementers should frame OPR features relative to Open Science objectives when describing or assessing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for explicit definition/schema (absence of standardized definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is neither a standardized definition nor an agreed schema of OPR features and implementations; the literature contains numerous overlapping and contradictory definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this ambiguity, the paper systematically collects definitions (n=122) to quantify variation over time, by subject area, and by material reviewed. Practitioners and evaluators should explicitly state which traits they are using when invoking 'open peer review.'
